vulnerabilities.title: HTML/CSS/JS Preview Tool with Unrestricted Execution
vulnerabilities.description: The preview-html tool uses srcDoc={rendered} with sandbox='allow-scripts' to intentionally render user-provided HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. While this is the intended design for this specific calculator tool, it represents a security boundary. The iframe sandbox attribute provides containment, but allow-scripts permits arbitrary JavaScript execution within that sandbox.
vulnerabilities.cwe: CWE-95 (Improper Neutralization of Directives in Dynamically Evaluated Code)
vulnerabilities.context: This is a design choice for a code preview tool. The FAQ explicitly states this is meant to execute JavaScript. Risk is mitigated by iframe sandbox attribute which prevents access to parent document, cookies, localStorage of main site.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: ACCEPT as designed feature. Consider: (1) Add Content Security Policy headers, (2) Document the sandbox limitations clearly, (3) Monitor for abuse patterns, (4) Consider adding optional code size limits if not present

vulnerabilities.title: dangerouslySetInnerHTML with Static Theme Script
vulnerabilities.description: Uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML to inject theme initialization script. However, this is safe because the script content is a static, hardcoded string (line 1) that doesn't include any user input or dynamic content.
vulnerabilities.risk: None - the injected script is entirely static and controlled by the application
vulnerabilities.recommendation: No action required. This is a safe use of dangerouslySetInnerHTML since the content is hardcoded. Consider adding a comment explaining why dangerouslySetInnerHTML is safe here for future maintainers.

configuration_issues.title: Public Environment Variables via NEXT_PUBLIC_ Prefix
configuration_issues.description: Uses NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefixed environment variables which are exposed to the browser. This is the correct pattern for Next.js since these are meant to be public (Google AdSense Client ID and Google Analytics Measurement ID are intended to be public).

strengths.description: Implements safe expression evaluation WITHOUT using eval(). Uses custom tokenizer and recursive descent parser. Whitelist of allowed math functions (sin, cos, sqrt, etc). No dynamic code execution.
strengths.recommendation: Excellent security practice - maintain this pattern

strengths.description: Validates key format with regex: /^[a-z0-9_]+$/i - only allows alphanumeric and underscores
Uses same key validation pattern as memory helper
Uses spawnSync() instead of shell execution, avoiding shell injection. Temporary files use crypto.randomBytes() for unique names. Proper cleanup in finally block.

summary.details: This is a calculator/utility website with no backend authentication or database access. The codebase follows secure coding practices with proper input validation, safe expression evaluation without eval(), and correct use of Next.js security features. The HTML preview tool is intentionally designed to execute user code within a sandboxed iframe for its intended purpose. No hardcoded secrets, credentials, or API keys were found. The main recommendation is to ensure CSP headers are properly configured and dependencies are kept up to date.
